stage: one whose self is yoked in the yoga of Brahman
description: The happiness found in the self by one unattached to external contacts; with the self yoked in the yoga of Brahman he enjoys imperishable happiness (akṣaya sukha) — contrasted with contact-born enjoyments, which have a beginning and an end (5.22).

stage: the yogin who has become Brahman (brahmabhūta)
description: Happiness within (antaḥsukha), delight within (antarārāma) and light within (antarjyotis): the yogin who has these, having become Brahman, attains brahma-nirvāṇa.

stage: the yogin of restrained mind practising the yoga of the self
description: The simile handed down for the restrained mind of the yogin: a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker.

stage: the yogin whose mind is stilled by the practice of yoga
description: The state called yoga: the mind stilled (niruddha) by practice comes to rest; seeing the self by the self one is content in the self; one knows boundless (ātyantika) happiness grasped by the intellect and beyond the senses, and established in it does not waver from the truth; having gained it one counts no other gain greater, and is not shaken even by heavy sorrow; it is the disconnection from union with suffering.

stage: the calmed, stainless yogin who has become Brahman
description: The highest happiness (sukham uttamam) that comes to the yogin whose mind is calmed and whose rajas is stilled, who has become Brahman and is stainless; always yoking himself he easily attains the boundless happiness of contact with Brahman (brahma-saṃsparśa).

stage: the one whose self is yoked in yoga
description: Seeing the same everywhere: the self abiding in all beings and all beings in the self (6.29); seeing the Lord everywhere and everything in him, so that neither is lost to the other (6.30); worshipping the Lord as abiding in all beings, established in oneness (6.31).

Arjuna's report of the mind in practice: restless, turbulent, strong and obstinate, its restraint as hard as restraining the wind, so that the steady standing of the yoga of sameness cannot be seen; the Lord grants that it is hard to restrain and restless, and says it is held by practice and dispassion.
